extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature (scientists, academics, and professional readers); also job applicants for academic/teaching posts
extracted.subtask_description: Writing and evaluating an academic book review (here: archaeology/classical studies) for a scientific/learned journal; includes assessing scholarship, use of evidence, argumentation, form, and illustrations. Also contains contemporaneous job-ad procedural standards for academic appointments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of archaeological evidence vs historical synthesis
rubrics_metrics.description: The author seems to exaggerate unduly the value of archaeological research and archaeological results; Etruscan pot-sherds and the debris of terramari are valuable in their way, but our sense of their value must not allow us to pooh-pooh the work of a great constructive historian like Mommsen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance archaeological data with constructive historical synthesis; do not dismiss established historians or overvalue raw archaeological finds at the expense of broader historical analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extent and thoroughness of scholarship
rubrics_metrics.description: His learning is incontestable. It ranges from Rome to Berlin, and from St. Petersburg to London; it includes at once the work of Prof. Conway on Italic dialects and the researches of Mr. Arthur Evans and Mr. J. L. Myres on prehistoric Greece.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive, wide-ranging familiarity with primary and secondary literature is a major strength; exhaustive synthesis of accumulated knowledge is praiseworthy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form, editing, and avoidance of workshop material
rubrics_metrics.description: The author has been so much interested in his matter that he has forgotten its form. He repeats himself, for instance, again and again, and one comes to notice ... the information (some four times repeated) that Pliny narrates the capture of 300 towns ... The author lets us too much into the workshop, and shows us too much rude workmanship and too little finished work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polish structure and editing; remove repetitive passages and 'scaffolding' so that argument and exposition appear as finished work rather than raw workshop notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of excessive polemics and diatribes
rubrics_metrics.description: He wastes not a few pages, and exhausts not a little the patience of the reader, by continual diatribes and disproofs, which may cause a flutter in the dovecots of Italian archaeology, but end by annoying the uninitiated scholar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refrain from prolonged polemics; critique should be restrained and aimed at clarity rather than rancour, to avoid alienating general readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for conclusions with sound arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: The author is somewhat too prone to risqué conclusions, which he is not averse to supporting by dubious arguments. Though he is ready, upon occasion, to controvert Sergi, he accepts without reluctance the most hazardous of his conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure major conclusions are justified by robust, well-supported arguments; avoid relying on dubious or speculative chains of inference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate weighting and consistency among different types of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: He exalts the evidence of skulls far above the testimony of language; to support it he is willing to accept the most dubious of linguistic evidence, and to connect the language of the Basques with that of the Berbers, or, indeed, with that of the hieroglyphics of Egypt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weigh archaeological, linguistic, and other evidence appropriately and consistently; do not privilege one kind of evidence in a way that forces acceptance of implausible auxiliary claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal consistency in comparative claims
rubrics_metrics.description: While he compares the archaeological relics of the Etruscans with those of south-western Asia Minor, he compares their language with the dialects of the north-east.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain internal consistency when relating material culture and linguistic/ethnic hypotheses; avoid drawing comparisons that point in inconsistent geographic/directional ways without explanation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity about conjectural vs established claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Professor Modestov's work ... is a learned if somewhat conjectural attempt to reconstruct by the aid of archaeological evidence the history of prehistoric Italy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly distinguish between speculative reconstruction and well-established conclusions; warn readers where claims are conjectural.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usefulness and quality of illustrations
rubrics_metrics.description: We should not be ungrateful for the many illustrations, for the most part original, with which the author has ornamented his book and sought to aid his readers. The Etruscan illustrations are particularly interesting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-quality, original illustrations are valuable—especially for archaeological and antiquarian subjects—and enhance the work's utility for readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensiveness and synthesis value
rubrics_metrics.description: Basing himself on the work of Italian archæologists, which for the most part lies buried in the pages of periodicals, he begins with the Palaeolithic age, and ends with the arrival of the Etruscans ... Ever'y scholar must be grateful for this laborious and exhaustive synthesis of the knowledge accumulated, during the last forty or fifty years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A thorough, synthetic account that brings together scattered literature is an important scholarly contribution and is positively evaluated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission procedure (official forms, deadlines, testimonials)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for these posts must be made on Forms to be obtained from the Education Department (Secondary), County Hall, Wakefield, where they must be returned not later than 9 a.m. Monday, June 17, 1937. Copies of not more than three recent testimonials must be sent with the application. Candidates applying through the post for the form of application should enclose a stamped and addressed envelope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the stated procedural requirements precisely: obtain and use the official form, observe deadlines, include at most the specified number of testimonials, and provide a stamped addressed envelope when requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Canvassing disqualifies applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Canvassing will be a disqualification. / Canvassing, either directly or indirectly, will be held to be a disqualification for employment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid any form of canvassing (direct or indirect); doing so will disqualify an application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum academic and subject qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must be graduates of a British University and possess good qualifications in German and one or both of the following subjects:—Mathematics, Domestic Science. / Candidates must be University graduates with teaching experience; preference will be given to applicants who hold a diploma in teaching. / They must possess a good general education, and, if possible, a knowledge of Chemistry and of Mechanics and Physics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Possess the specified university degree(s), subject specializations, and where indicated a teaching diploma or specific subject knowledge; match the post's listed academic requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching experience and demonstrable fitness for post
rubrics_metrics.description: Teaching experience is essential. / Candidates must have experience as teachers: preference will be given to applicants who hold a diploma in teaching.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrable prior teaching experience (and diplomas where preferred) is required or will be favourably considered for appointment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Age and physical condition requirements for overseas posts
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates should not be less than 13 nor over 30 years of age, have a robust constitution, and have taken a University Degree in Honours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe any stated age limits and physical/health requirements for overseas or particular appointments (note: use the advert's original wording when applying).

rubrics_metrics.name: Terms of service (salary, commencement, hours, vacations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Salary, £a95 per annum (L.Eg. 14 per mensem), rising to £393 per annum (L.Eg. 3a per mensem). Allowance for passage out to Egypt. Teaching hours, on an average, four daily, Fridays only excepted. Summer vacation not less than two months. / Duties to commence in September next. / Commencing salary, £350 a year, rising by annual increments ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should note and accept the stated salary scales, allowances, commencement dates, working hours, and vacation terms as part of the conditions of the post.
